name: Vue
subtitle: Progressive UI framework
creator: Evan You
description: A framework for building UIs with HTML-based templates and reactive state. You can adopt it gradually, from one widget on a page to a full single-page app. Single-File Components keep template, logic and styles together in one .vue file.

languages.youWrite: HTML templates plus JavaScript or TypeScript in .vue files

concepts.explanation: Template, script and style in one .vue file.
v-if, v-for, v-model and @click in templates.
ref and reactive make values that update the UI.
Derived values that cache until inputs change.
Organize logic by feature with setup functions.
Pass data down, send events up.
Opt-in compile mode without a virtual DOM (3.6).

codeSamples.label: Vue SFC
codeSamples.code:
<script setup>
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
const count = ref(0)
const double = computed(() => count.value * 2)
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="count++">Count: {{ count }} (x2 = {{ double }})</button>
</template>

pairsWith.reason: Build tool by the same author

pros: Gentle learning curve and excellent documentation
Official router and state libraries reduce decision fatigue
Works as a sprinkle-in or a full framework
High satisfaction: 84% in State of JS 2025
cons: The Vue 2 to 3 migration was painful
Two API styles split tutorials and examples
Template type inference still has rough edges
